prompts.fix-fresh:
Use case: AI-illustrated visual guide that helps a beginner fishkeeper recognise what is wrong with their fish. Photorealistic educational aquarium photography, NOT cartoons, icons, vector drawings, watercolor, plastic 3D renders or poster typography. Realistic underwater macro-photography aesthetic: anatomically believable fish, natural scales, translucent fins, restrained aquarium light, softly blurred home-aquarium background. Each cell names its fish and its scene. The fish is sharp, in focus, level and natural (not twisted at odd angles), large in its cell and fully in view. The key feature in each cell must be OBVIOUS to a novice at thumbnail size, while staying believable (no horror, no gore, no giant parasites). Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, watermarks, arrows or symbols anywhere in the image.
STRICT CONTACT SHEET for cropping into twelve separate pictures: exactly FOUR equal-width columns and THREE equal-height rows, twelve equal square cells covering the complete image edge to edge. No gutters, no borders, no outer margin. Every cell is its own separate scene with its own background. Nothing crosses a cell boundary; keep the whole subject inside the central 85 percent of its cell. Never put a cell's feature into another cell. Follow the exact row-major order below.
Row 1 column 1: a red-and-white FANTAIL GOLDFISH in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, its WHITE areas evenly coated with a clearly visible fine GOLD-YELLOW velvety DUST over the whole back, sides and fins, standing out clearly against the body, like the fish was lightly dusted with gold powder, catching the side light; far finer than salt grains, no separate white spots; fins clamped (velvet).
Row 1 column 2: a NEON TETRA in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, the whole small fish in side view filling the cell, one eye clearly BULGING OUT like a marble, slightly cloudy (popeye).
Row 1 column 3: a NEON TETRA in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, body level and in sharp focus, swimming fast sideways and RUBBING its flank against a smooth round rock, skin slightly hazy, a faint swirl of sand (flashing).
Row 1 column 4: a bronze CORY catfish on sand in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, side view, its TAIL FIN clearly DAMAGED: a big ragged NOTCH bitten out of the top half of the tail so the background shows through the gap; body healthy (fin injury).
Row 2 column 1: a panda CORY catfish in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, LYING FLAT ON ITS SIDE on the sand, one side of its body facing up, fins limp, unable to stay upright (balance problem).
Row 2 column 2: a bristlenose PLECO in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, sharp and in focus, rubbing the side of its head and body against a smooth piece of driftwood, its skin slightly hazy and greyish, fins flared (flashing).
Row 2 column 3: a common PLECO in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, side view resting on sand, its belly clearly and smoothly SWOLLEN, round and tight like an over-full belly, the swelling part of its own body (dropsy; catfish have no scales to pinecone).
Row 2 column 4: a black MOLLY in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, FLOATING ON ITS SIDE right at the water surface, one flank facing up, fins splayed, unable to stay upright; the water surface line across the top (swim bladder).
Row 3 column 1: a plain dark navy-blue African mbuna CICHLID with no yellow anywhere, near rocks in a freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, evenly coated with a clearly visible fine GOLD-YELLOW velvety DUST over the whole back, sides and fins, standing out clearly against the body, like the fish was lightly dusted with gold powder, catching the side light; far finer than salt grains, no separate white spots; fins clamped (velvet).
Row 3 column 2: a female GUPPY (plain grey body, small tail) in a planted freshwater home aquarium, softly blurred dark teal-green plants behind, the WHOLE FISH in side view, normal shape, its eye normal size and NOT bulging, but the eye covered by an obvious MILKY WHITE-GREY FILM like frosted glass, so the dark pupil barely shows (cloudy eye).

review.method: Every cell of fix-fresh, fix-mixed and fix-repair opened at full sheet size and compared with the published crop it would replace (or the pond first take); a retake is used only when it is clearly better.
review.used: 22 crops: 10 freshwater (gold dust now obvious on a red-and-white goldfish, neon popeye/flukes framed cleanly, cory tail notch and cory on its side clear, sharp pleco rubbing driftwood, gold dust on a dark African, guppy cloudy eye now a whole female guppy with a frosted eye vs guppy popeye seen head-on with the eye sticking out), fish-neutral step-pea (tweezers + saucer of peas, no fish) and step-watch (calm tank in a living room, notebook), 3 marine (clear red sores on chromis and orchid dottyback, dottyback flukes level and in focus), emerald crab missing a claw, hermit after acclimation, plus from fix-repair: pleco dropsy (side view, belly part of the body), watchman goby swollen (natural), black molly flat on its side at the surface, cleaner shrimp with leg stubs, and two pond KHV pictures that replace the first takes (closed gill covers, no gaping wound).
